headline: MCA draft reportedly makes CSR impact assessment voluntary for ₹10 crore+ firms
summary_points: Reported: MCA has issued a draft that makes CSR impact assessment voluntary.
Reported: the draft ends the mandatory assessment for firms with CSR obligations of ₹10 crore or more.
The measure is a draft; final rules, notification number and effective date are not yet known.
Full text of the draft was not available, so exact provisions and amendments are unconfirmed.
who_is_affected: Companies with average CSR obligations of ₹10 crore or more, their CSR committees, and implementing agencies and consultants who provide impact assessments.
action_required: Review the MCA draft on the official website, consider submitting comments within the consultation period, and continue current assessments until the rules are finalised.

social.linkedin:
MCA draft proposes to make CSR impact assessment voluntary.

According to a report by The CSR Universe, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs has put out a draft that would end the mandatory impact assessment for companies with CSR obligations of ₹10 crore or more.

What we know so far:
- The change is reported to be in a draft stage, not yet final.
- The notification number, effective date and the exact rule amendments are not yet confirmed.

Why it matters:
Companies, CSR committees and implementing agencies may need to revisit budgets and reporting practices for impact assessments once the rules are finalised.

Until the final notification is issued, existing requirements continue to apply. Companies may also want to consider giving feedback during the consultation window.

This update is based on a news report. Please verify the details with the official MCA source before acting.
